quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Human resources specialists recruit, screen, interview or place individuals within an organisation.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Human Resources Specialists) include Corporate Recruiter, HR Generalist, HR Coordinator and Human Resources Specialist.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What a human resources specialist does
paragraphs: Human resources specialists recruit, screen, interview or place individuals within an organisation.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Human Resources Specialists. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Hire employees and process the paperwork that goes with hiring.
Tell job applicants about duties, pay, benefits and schedules.
Explain human resources policies, procedures, laws and regulations.
Handle employee relations issues such as work complaints.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.
O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: BBA (Bachelor of Business Administration); MBA (Master of Business Administration).
Less common routes on the map: BA (Bachelor of Arts); B.Com (Bachelor of Commerce).
